definition: Facial disfigurement is a visible difference in the face, such as a congenital malformation like cleft lip and/or palate. In the supplied psychology context, it is discussed as a facial difference that can change how observers visually attend to a face and how positively they appraise it.

reasons: The packet supports that congenital facial malformation (e.g., cleft lip/palate) affects adults’ visual scanning and subjective appraisal of infant faces, but it does not explicitly define “facial disfigurement” as a general “visible difference in the face.”

The packet describes the effect as “adversely affected” and discusses “aversive behaviour” / cuteness ratings; it does not support the specific framing that observers’ appraisal changes “how positively they appraise it.”

The definition equates the general term “facial disfigurement” with “cleft lip and/or palate,” but the packet discusses “cleft-affected infant faces” and does not explicitly map the broader term to that example as a definition.
The packet supports congenital facial malformation examples such as cleft lip and/or palate, but it does not explicitly define facial disfigurement as any “visible difference in the face.”

The claim that facial disfigurement “can change how observers visually attend to a face and how positively they appraise it” goes beyond the packet’s wording and generalizes a study finding about cleft-affected infant faces into a broader definitional statement.
The definition should stay tightly tied to the packet’s specific sense (cleft-affected infant faces / congenital facial malformation) rather than presenting broader, unsupported general wording.
